newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Impala Platinum lifts attributable income.
newsitem.headline: Impala Platinum lifts attributable income.

text.p: South Africa's Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd lifted attributable profit for the six months to end-December 1996 by 3.4 percent to 95.9 million rand from 92.7 million rand.
But the company said it did not expect performance in the second half of the year to exceed the results it reported on Tuesday.
"Performance in the second half of the year is not likely to exceed the level reported for the first half," Implats said.

Implats -- South Africa's second-largest platinum producer -- said it increased output of refined platinum to 499,000 ounces in the half year under review from 491,000 in the corresponding six months in 1995.

But on the negative side, Implats said it sustained a loss of more than 100 million rand as a result of forward cover losses accumulated last year when the company fixed $193 million of anticipated year receipts at 3.92 rand to the dollar.

"The forward dollar sales position at the end of the previous financial year resulted in an opportunity loss of revenue for the period of more than 100 million rand. No forward cover was in place at the end of December 1996," the company said.
Implats reported earnings per share of 154 cents against the 149 cents in the corresponding period in 1995. It declared an unchanged interim dividend of 30 cents.
Analysts polled by Reuters had forecast a concensus arnings per share of 120.0 with the range 110.0-155.0 and a dividend of 30.0 cents.

Implats said sales revenue increased by 7 percent which was pushed along by a 11 percent depreciation in the rand/dollar exchange rate and marginally higher sales volumes for all major metals -- except platinum.
"The positive impact of the weaker rand and additional volumes was substantially eroded by the fall in metal prices," the company said.
Cost of sales at 1.12 billion rand was an increase of six percent on the six months to end-December 1995.

And on-mine costs per kg of platinum group metals extracted increased by 15 percent to 32,500 rand/kg from 28,200, mainly due to increased labour costs and additional costs incurred in building up production at the group's 11 and 14 shafts.

Implats said, although fundamentals still supported a stronger platinum price in the medium and longer term, it did not anticipate any material recovery in metal prices for the remainder of the financial year.
"The negative gold sentiment and the dogged reaction of the platinum price to movements in the gold price depresses the short term outlook on platinum," Implats said.
